import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.cluster import AgglomerativeClustering

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Identify strong candidates based on t-statistics
    t_stats = [abs(stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==1, feats.column(fid)], 
                                  feats.x[feats.y==0, feats.column(fid)], 
                                  equal_var=False)[0]) 
               for fid in feats.ids]
    
    # Sort by t-statistic descending
    sorted_idx = np.argsort(t_stats)[::-1]
    strong_features = [feats.ids[i] for i in sorted_idx[:20]]
    
    # Find correlated pairs with |r| >= 0.6
    correlated_pairs = []
    for i in range(len(strong_features)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(strong_features)):
            corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, feats.column(strong_features[i])], 
                              feats.x[:, feats.column(strong_features[j])])[0,1]
            if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                correlated_pairs.append((strong_features[i], strong_features[j]))
    
    # Cluster correlated features using Agglomerative Clustering
    if correlated_pairs:
        feature_set = set()
        for a, b in correlated_pairs:
            feature_set.add(a)
            feature_set.add(b)
        
        # Create feature matrix for clustering
        feature_list = list(feature_set)
        X = feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in feature_list]]
        
        # Use hierarchical clustering to group correlated features
        clustering = AgglomerativeClustering(n_clusters=None, 
                                            distance_threshold=1-0.6,
                                            linkage='average')
        clusters = clustering.fit_predict(X.T)
        
        # Select representative feature from each cluster (highest t-statistic)
        cluster_representatives = {}
        for i, cluster_id in enumerate(clusters):
            fid = feature_list[i]
            t_stat = t_stats[sorted_idx.index(feats.ids.index(fid))]
            if cluster_id not in cluster_representatives or \
               t_stat > cluster_representatives[cluster_id][1]:
                cluster_representatives[cluster_id] = (fid, t_stat)
        
        # Get final drivers from representatives
        drivers = [fid for fid, _ in cluster_representatives.values()]
        drivers = sorted(drivers, key=lambda x: t_stats[feats.ids.index(x)], reverse=True)
    else:
        # No strong correlations; use top features directly
        drivers = [feats.ids[i] for i in sorted_idx[:min(MAX_DRIVERS, len(feats.ids))]]
    
    # Return design with top drivers and all features for regression
    return Design(
        drivers=tuple(drivers[:MAX_DRIVERS]),
        columns=feats.ids,
        products=(),
        loadings={}
    )
